ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in Figure 11, rod AB rotates about point A with constant angular velocity, and drives the small ring of mass M sleeved on the smooth horizontal rod OC to move. At the beginning of the motion, rod AB is in the vertical position, then how does the velocity of small ring M change?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the left side is a vertical support line, point A is below, and point O is directly above it; from O to the right there is a horizontal smooth rod OC. The vertical distance from A to the horizontal rod OC is marked as h. The inclined rod AB rotates about point A, passes through the small ring M on the horizontal rod, and the small ring M can only move horizontally along the horizontal rod OC; the arrow and ω in the figure indicate that rod AB rotates with constant angular velocity. Reasoning: According to the specified method, take A as the origin, vertically upward as the y-axis, and horizontally to the right as the x-axis. From the image it can be known that small ring M is located on the horizontal rod OC, so its trajectory is the straight line y=h; at the same time small ring M is also the intersection point of the rotating rod AB and the straight line y=h. Let the angle through which rod AB has rotated from the initial vertical position be θ; because the angular velocity is constant, θ=ωt. For intersection point M, the geometric relation is tanθ=x/h, therefore the horizontal displacement of the small ring is x=h tanθ. Differentiate with respect to time: v=dx/dt=hωsec²(ωt). After the motion begins, θ gradually increases, and within the shown range of motion sec²θ increases as θ increases, so the velocity of small ring M gradually increases. Final answer: gradually increase.
